title: Brazil youth player banned for mimicking monkey gesture after reporting racist abuse
content:
The Brazil football federation (CBF) has appealed a sanction handed to Under-17 player Eduardo Conceicao after he was banned for four months for mimicking a monkey gesture in protest against the racist abuse he reported he received.

Brazil youth international Eduardo, 16, reported that he was targeted with racist abuse by Argentine Matheo Benitez during April’s South American Under-17 Championship group stage fixture between Brazil and Argentina. He scored Brazil’s third goal in a 3-0 win in the 89th minute and, outraged over a perceived lack of action over the abuse, celebrated by mimicking a monkey gesture towards Benitez in protest.

Television footage showed the Brazilian players complaining to the referee, who, however, did not enforce the anti-racism protocol. The incident was also reflected in the match delegate’s report following a request from Brazil.

In May, Conmebol gave an identical four-month ban to both Eduardo and Benitez.

The players received the bans in accordance with the South American football federation’s disciplinary code in relation to discrimination.

Article 15.1 of Conmebol’s disciplinary code states: “Any player or official who insults or violates the human dignity of another person or group of people, by any means, based on skin color, race, sex or sexual orientation, ethnicity, language, creed or origin, disability, political affiliation or ideology, economic status, place of birth, or any other status or reason, shall be suspended for a minimum of ten matches or for a minimum period of four months.”

Eduardo plays for Brazilian side Palmeiras at club level. The forward has represented the team’s under-20 side this year and has been linked with a number of Europe’s top sides. Palmeiras are working with the CBF to present Eduardo’s appeal.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has also appealed the sanction.

The CBF, AFA and Conmebol have been approached by The Athletic for comment.
